item.title: Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Production Systems: Empirical Evidence, Implementation Pipelines, and Industrial Applications
item.content:encoded:
Ruoqi Geng, Cardiff University

Di Li, Warwick University

Yang Cheng, Aalborg University

Artificial intelligence is rapidly moving from a standalone analytics tool to an operational capability that reshapes how production systems are planned, controlled, and improved in real time. In production contexts, AI can be understood as digital technologies performing tasks and decisions traditionally associated with human intelligence. Recent operations and production research highlights that AI's operational value increasingly depends on data availability, interoperability, and sharing across heterogeneous systems, enabling AI to sense, learn, and act within production environments rather than merely supporting off-line analysis.

Appel publié par Production Planning & Control. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • AI-Augmented Production Planning and Control: predictive and prescriptive analytics for production planning, sequencing, scheduling, and dispatching; reinforcement learning and autonomous decision-making for factory operations; AI-supported capacity management and workflow optimisation
  • Business–AI Alignment and AI Readiness Pipeline for Production Systems: translation of production decisions into AI use cases and data requirements; data governance, quality monitoring, preparation, cleaning, and integration; measures of AI readiness
  • AI-enabled Quality and Process Control: machine learning and deep learning for defect detection and predictive quality control; sensor data and image analytics for automated inspection; AI-driven adaptive process regulation
  • Agentic and Workflow-Oriented Deployment in Production: AI-enabled workflows connecting data preparation to production decisions; natural-language interfaces and AI-assisted decision support; production agents operationalising decision guidance
  • AI-Enabled Cyber–Physical Production Systems and Digital Twins: intelligent digital twins for real-time optimisation; hybrid physics–AI approaches; continuous learning and data synchronisation; edge AI for decentralised decision-making; human–robot collaboration
  • AI and Additive Manufacturing: generative design and topology optimisation; AI-enabled defect prediction and build-path optimisation; distributed AM network coordination; end-user leverage of AI for customisation
  • AI and Blockchain for Production Systems: AI-enhanced traceability and secure data sharing; AI-blockchain integration for auditability and transparency; smart contracts in production automation
  • Human–AI Interaction and Organisational Transformation: human-in-the-loop AI and operator–AI collaboration; organisational readiness and capability development; explainability, trust, transparency, and governance mechanisms
  • Empirical Innovations in Data, Measurement, and Evaluation: field experiments, industry datasets, IoT streams, and digital twin logs; measurable improvements in productivity, quality, flexibility, and decision accuracy
  • Extended Production Contexts: AI in warehousing and fulfilment operations; AI-enabled autonomous mobile robots; real-time slotting and vision systems for object recognition

item.title: Hybrid Human-AI Collaborative Networks
item.content:encoded:
Rosanna Fornasiero, CNR IEIIT

Luis M. Camarinha-Matos, NOVA University Lisbon

Xavier Boucher, Mines Saint-Étienne

Angel Ortiz, Universitat Politècnica de València

Hybrid Collaborative Networks (HCNs), involving human-AI collaboration, are emerging as central to value creation in digitally enabled, globally distributed and socio-technically managed ecosystems. Based on the complex interplay between humans and artificial intelligence, these networks combine very heterogeneous actors—such as organizations, individuals, intelligent systems, embodied AI, and platforms—interacting across physical, digital, and organizational boundaries.

Understanding the dynamics of such networks is critical to ensure their design, management, resilience, adaptability and sustained performance in rapidly changing environments. Analysing and managing the dynamic nature of HCNs includes examining how hybrid collaborative structures emerge, evolve, adapt, and dissolve over time. The dynamics of interactive performance and role distribution for such networks, but also the change of collaboration patterns over time, together with the managerial frameworks required to ensure adaptive governance of HCNs open strong scientific challenges, where technological added-value should be deeply associated with socio-human approaches.

Appel publié par Production Planning & Control. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Digital platforms for HCNs
  • Collaborative dynamics among human and AI teams
  • Agile design and management of hybrid networks
  • Design of AI teammates
  • Knowledge life cycle in distributed cognitive systems
  • Collaboration and coopetition in untrustworthy environments
  • Life cycle of collaborative cognitive cyber-physical systems
  • Combination of human expertise with AI systems
  • Scalability and adaptability of HCNs
  • Collective decision making, value creation and creativity
  • Digital twins for HCNs
  • Governance framework for HCNs
  • Understanding and explainability of HCN decisions
  • Advanced collaborative robotics
  • Complex hybridization of collaboration – organizations, people, smart machines, intelligent systems
  • Resilience & antifragility in HCNs
  • Ethics, security, & trust in HCNs
  • AI integration for logistics and transportation networks
  • AI for collaborative risk and crisis management
  • Society 5.0 and collaborative networks
  • CN applications and case studies in multiple fields
